evidence: Mean outbreak size on a tree is a pairwise-distance polynomial, but the full outbreak law determines the strictly richer connected-set size-and-boundary profile. Lanchier–La Salle develops finite-graph moment bounds, not tree-topology identifiability; published generalized-cospectral tree thresholds involve distinct spectral invariants. An earlier mathematical study of source identification inside a fixed known tree concerns distinguishability of *source vertices* from mean curves, whereas the present result concerns distinguishability of *trees* from complete distributions with the source unobserved. Another graph-study concerns reversals of mean outbreak comparisons rather than complete equality.

value.rationale: A natural inverse problem asks whether perfect all-transmissibility outbreak statistics determine a finite tree contact topology when the infecting source is unobserved. The sharp eleven-vertex first failure with a unique same-degree collision refutes even complete distributional identification. The exact size/boundary profile supplies a transferable structural explanation, and this is not a fixed-parameter counterexample or a known moment-only computation. Finite cutoff is natural and complete; limitations to this precise sampling model acknowledged.
